title: The gate ladder: affected checks per task, the full gate and tree scanners per phase, CI under eight minutes
description: The same full set of checks runs per task, per phase, locally and in CI several times, and the set is large because the product carries its own tree lints as tests. Measured: a task gate in the dogfood plan took 716 s, of which the sweep was 384 s and the panel browser gate 282 s; a narrow task gate measured 1,327 s because derived affected steps re-ran 506 s of suites its own full-sweep key had already run; the sweep is 6 min 36 s of wall and 34.6 min of CPU, and CI runs take 12 to 15 minutes. The CI half of this ladder (one executable gate description, skip of a green SHA, the codec cells) is already the earlier F1 phase's; this phase adds the per-task and per-phase rungs and the remaining speed.
desiredOutcome: A task's gate is the selection of checks its change affects, trusted only after its miss rate was measured on this repository's history; tree scanners and the full gate, browser steps included, run once per phase and on push, never per task; a probe of the guarded lints runs at sign-off only when the phase changed them; the sweep's wall clock is under four minutes and CI is under eight minutes and 55 runner-minutes, each measured with the same command before and after; one commit verb writes the index and the shard together, so adding a task mid-phase never leaves the plan uncommittable; and red-first through a sweep-shaped command proves when the task's suites pass.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause: acceptance (5) 'the measured result over 20 commits is recorded in the task outcome with the commit range'. The outcome records a 2-commit window (ad586f07b..d33730d60) in which one commit timed out at 1200s (NOT MEASURED) and the other was a full-set selection ('so no suite can be missed'), giving 'misses 0 of 1 commits (mutation); 0 of 1 runs (CI)'. That is zero evidence about the miss rate and not the 20-commit measurement the clause asks for; the executor itself says the 20-commit run is 'still owed by the orchestrator'. The 'misses 0 of 1' line must not be read as a clean miss rate.
findings.resolution: Run the 20-commit command the outcome names on a quiet machine (python3 tools/measure-affected-miss.py --commits 20 --budget-minutes 240 --timeout 2400 --ci-limit 30 --json) and record its output and commit range in the outcome before the task closes done; or, if the orchestrator decides the measurement is out of scope for this task, split it into its own task rather than close this one as met. If the task is closed with no change (--no-change --reason), the reason must say acceptance (5) is unmeasured.
findings.acceptedReason: P142 delivered the gate ladder: affected selection per task, the full gate and scanners per phase, the one commit verb and red-first through a sweep, plus the fixes the phase review and adversarial rounds asked for, and a lint probe that runs its rows in parallel worker trees so a phase-wide probe fits the sign-off bound. Three meds are left as recorded. R1: the miss measurement was taken over 20 of 26 commits and found misses (D13), so promoting the selection to the task gate moved to P143.1, gated on P143.4 and a 0-miss re-measurement. R9: the per-block cost split needs true per-block costs, so it moved to P143.6, because the re-recorded table cannot balance the shards today. R10: the sweep under 4 minutes moved to 3.8.0 (D13) as P143.5. Lows are carried to BUG-29-dau. Per-task reviewer answers continued over: P142.8 intent diverges: P142.8 diverges on acceptance (1) and the cost table: the split itself is correct and every case is kept (reviewer-verified). Under-240s is carried by P142.11-6yq (R10); the cost table is re-recorded from the Windows CI cell logs with --costs-from-log after the ci/P142 run, since a recording from this Mac would understate Windows timeouts (R9). Lows R11, R12 go to the batch.; P142.11-6yq intent diverges: P142.11 diverges on acceptance (1): measured 385.3/385.4 s vs 240 s on a quiet machine (HEAD 415.8/416.1). Block scheduling (Part 2) matches; Part 1 cut only one repeat. Med findings go to P142.14-6yq (timeout case, stale docs) and BUG-30-6yq (product temp-dir leak); the remaining gap to 240 s needs less total work in tests/test_drive_phase.py and goes to the owner as a design decision.; P142.13-6yq red-first not-proved: orchestrator proved le1-le3 red: runner_line_end_violations crippled to return [] in a git-archive copy of HEAD 0544c08c -> 170/173, le1/le2/le3 FAIL; le4 (live tree quiet) correctly stays green; sf12/sf13 red-first proved by the helper; P142.45-6yq intent diverges: The 6 findings of P142.45 are handed to P142.47, which redesigns the redo to move no tree. Every finding sits in the move machinery that task deletes.

findings.issue: P142.3's description is a verbatim re-ask of a task already done (b52ba79a, amended 66b3635d): tools/measure-affected-miss.py has existed since P131.16-dau, so this task adds nothing and its tests.add entries are met only by pre-existing cases m6, m8, m10, m13. A duplicate task in the plan is an input error that wastes an executor run and can double-count 'tests added'.
findings.resolution: Close P142.3 with --no-change and a reason naming b52ba79a/66b3635d and the pre-existing cases, after (5) is measured; or rewrite its description to the measurement alone.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "a phase touching no such file runs none and says so" / acceptance (2) "prints that it ran none" on the held path: a run that printed `ran none` is held as `state["lintProbe"] = {"head": head}` (the word is not stored), and the held branch then appends `lint probe green (held at this HEAD)` - so any re-entry at the same HEAD (e.g. after the sign-off verb stopped) reports a probe that ran no row as green, the exact reading-as-a-proof the clause forbids.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.12-6yq (e236bb23ae07): Store the word with the hold (`{"head": head, "said": "ran none"|"green"}`) and echo it on the held branch (`lint probe ran none (held at this HEAD)`); add an lp6 twin that holds a ran-none run and asserts the held did-line says ran none.

findings.issue: The success print breaks the module's stated invariant `INSTRUCTION_BYTES = 300` ("The bound every print that is not a stop stays inside") whenever a probe runs: the executor's own measurement is 312 bytes in lp1's one-task fixture. This repo keeps tools/prove-gates.py, so from this change every sign-off here prints past the bound; lp1 does not assert the bound and dp3 only measures a probeless fixture, so nothing goes red.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.12-6yq (e236bb23ae07): Make the probe clause fit (e.g. fold it into the `invariants clean` clause as `invariants clean, lint probe green|ran none`, or move the word into the sign-off summary) and extend dp3 (or lp1/lp2) to measure the success print of a probe-carrying fixture against INSTRUCTION_BYTES.

findings.issue: A shipped product script now executes any project file that happens to sit at `tools/prove-gates.py` at every sign-off, by filename convention alone, with no plan key opting in: a user project with an unrelated script at that path has it run with `--changed <paths>` and its exit 1 read as a not-proven stop and any other non-zero exit as a refusal that blocks sign-off. Every other gate the driver runs is named by the plan (meta.buildCommands, meta.runtimeBoot); this one is not. The executor flagged it as (b).
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.12-6yq (e236bb23ae07): Key the probe off the plan (a `meta.buildCommands` entry or a dedicated meta key naming the probe command and declaring it speaks the `--changed` protocol), absent means skip; set it in this repo's plan. If that is out of this task's files, file it as a fix task before sign-off rather than shipping the filename convention.

findings.issue: Acceptance (4) is checked as equality of porcelain status letters + paths only. A file already dirty before the run (` M`) that the probe leaves mutated still reads ` M` after, so a stranded mutation in an already-modified lint file passes; conversely, a second session editing the shared checkout during the minutes-long run produces a false `left the checkout changed` stop whose remedy (`restore the tree`) would tell the operator to discard someone else's work.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.12-6yq (e236bb23ae07): For entries dirty before the run, also compare a content digest (git hash-object of each) before and after; and word the stop as 'changed during the probe run' naming the entries without prescribing a restore, or refuse to start the probe when a path in the changed set is already dirty.

findings.issue: `subprocess.run` of a minutes-long mutating probe carries no timeout, so a hung probe hangs the sign-off step indefinitely with the tree possibly mid-mutation.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.12-6yq (e236bb23ae07): Pass a timeout (a generous bound or one read from the plan), catch `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` as a refusal stop; the status comparison in `finally` already reports what a killed run left.

findings.issue: lp6's 'at another HEAD it runs once' twin calls `lint_probe(..., None)`, which short-circuits the hold on `if head and ...`; it never exercises a different SHA, so a hold that ignored the head comparison (e.g. `held.get("head")` truthy) would still pass lp6.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.12-6yq (e236bb23ae07): Call the twin with a different 40-hex head (`"b" * 40`) so the comparison itself is what lets it run.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'Split each into staged blocks so the sweep spreads them across workers, and re-record the cost table.' The table is untouched, so the four split files keep the figures they had when each ran unsplit on one slot. Those figures now set the shard balance and every split file's timeout. On the live table, shard 3/3 holds three staged suites in a row (test_close_phase 330.3, test__deps 268.2, test_stamp_verification 265.4). The per-block process overhead on Windows, where test_stamp_verification now starts a process for each of its blocks, has never been measured. The executor gives a reason (the table binds to windows-latest and cannot be recorded from darwin), but the clause is still not done.
findings.resolution: Make it a tracked task before sign-off. Once this lands on a CI run, save each Windows selftests cell's log and run `python tools/sweep-selftests.py --costs-from-log <logs> --platform windows-latest --record-costs .github/sweep-costs.json`. Then confirm that the shard split it prints is balanced and that no split file's calibrated timeout at held=3 sits within 2x of its measured wall time.

findings.file: tools/sweep-selftests.py:1361-1400 (the scheduler change); the bound is tests/test_drive_phase.py
findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'Acceptance: (1) time python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py is under 240 s wall on this machine twice, at least 20 minutes apart'. findings.issue: The diff makes three untouched documents state the old admission rule. CLAUDE.md says a staged suite 'is admitted with `stage_grant(jobs)` slots', CONTRIBUTING.md says 'is admitted holding `stage_grant(jobs)` slots', and the ci.yml comment says 'a staged suite is admitted holding all but one of them'. After slot_gate's change at tools/sweep-selftests.py:1385-1394, a suite holds as many slots as are free when its turn comes, between 1 and that number. The executor listed all three as stale and outside its files.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.28-6yq (e6813d0b0a18): Reword each to say: up to `stage_grant(jobs)` slots, as many as are free when its turn comes and at least one, with the number it holds passed to the child in SWEEP_STAGE_GRANT and its timeout calibrated to that number.

findings.issue: A staged suite's grant is fixed when it is admitted. If it is admitted with 1 slot, it runs every block serially (stage_workers=min(6,1)) for its whole run, even after other slots free up. Its timeout at held=1 is 3 x cost, which can exceed SWEEP_DEADLINE. tt5 still only bounds timeouts at the full grant, and its label was widened to accept that the deadline 'cuts ... a staged suite admitted late with fewer slots'. On today's windows table this is latent, not live. At jobs=4 the staged suite second in each shard gets 1 slot (shard 2/3: test_commit_task_work 222.9; shard 3/3: test__deps 268.2), and both serial costs are well under the 1380 s deadline. A rebalance that put test_audit_task (606.0) or test_drive_phase (1346.4) second in a shard would have the deadline cut a run that is slow, not hung, and nothing would turn red first.
findings.resolution: Add a tt5 sibling over the live table: for each `--shard i/3` at jobs=4, compute each staged suite's admitted slots (ticket order, with what is free at its turn, assuming earlier holders have not yet finished). Assert that file_timeout at those slots, and the serial cost it implies, stay under SWEEP_DEADLINE. That makes the latent case fail on the table change that creates it.

findings.file: tools/sweep-selftests.py:1761-1765 (one_block's timeout); cases tools/sweep-selftests.py:4007 bg6, :4306 tt0, :4321 tt1
findings.issue: The block path's timeout calibration, which every live staged suite now takes (stage_labels reads a literal STAGES in all eight: test__deps, test__output, test_audit_task, test_close_phase, test_commit_task_work, test_drive_phase, test_stamp_verification, check-committed-pii), is reached by no case with a non-empty cost table. bb1 and sr13 sweep with costs={}, sb1 with costs=None, so file_timeout returns the floor whatever one_block passes. bg6, tt0 and tt1 pin 'the timed-heavy staged suite gets its calibrated timeout and is told it' and 'an untimed staged suite gets the largest any entry would get', but their fixtures ('if False: staged_main()' with no STAGES) go through the whole-suite fallback only. Replacing :1763 with the bare floor `timeout`, or dropping staged=True, leaves the suite green. The task clause 'Keep per-block timeouts calibrated' has no case behind it.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.26-6yq (57fd38c4dff9): Add a case that sweeps a STAGES-literal fixture whose blocks print SWEEP_FILE_TIMEOUT, on jobs=4, once with costs={'split-suite': 900.0} (expect TIMEOUT_PER_COST*900//stage_grant(4) in every block's output, and the row's timeout) and once with a ghost-only table (expect the largest entry's figure, never the floor). Add a deadline variant like tt2 that shows a block's timeout cut to what is left. Prove it red by mutating :1763 to the floor.

findings.file: CLAUDE.md:239-243; CONTRIBUTING.md:330-334; .github/workflows/ci.yml:134-135; tools/sweep-selftests.py:1713 (sweep docstring), :1587-1590 (costs_from_rows docstring), :1604-1612 (record_costs 'about' text), :1474-1478 (shard comment)
findings.issue: These still describe the grant model the diff retired for every staged suite in the tree. CLAUDE.md says a staged_main suite 'is admitted with stage_grant(jobs) slots ... and is told the number in SWEEP_STAGE_GRANT, which sizes its block pool'. CONTRIBUTING.md and the ci.yml comment say the same. sweep()'s docstring says '`costs` orders the submissions (`run_order`)', but sweep() now orders by work_items. costs_from_rows, the shard comment and the record_costs 'about' string say the recorded figure is 'wall seconds times the slots ... the file held', but a block-run suite's figure is now the sum of its processes' seconds. The 'about' string is written into the committed .github/sweep-costs.json on the next --record-costs. The executor named the first three as followers, but no case and no task holds them.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.27-6yq (5ca403f01ad4): Rewrite each to the block model in this task or a follower task filed before sign-off: blocks are run as the sweep's jobs, one slot each, and replayed via --replay; a suite whose STAGES is not a literal runs whole on a grant; a block-run suite's cost is the summed slot-seconds of its processes. Fix sweep()'s docstring to name work_items.

findings.issue: sh6 says 'a shard runs its costliest files FIRST, so the slowest suite starts at once', but it asserts run_order(), which sweep() no longer calls. Submission order is now work_items (:1743). bb3 pins work_items as a function, but no case shows that sweep() submits in that order. Reverting :1743 to any other order leaves sh6 and bb3 green. bb1 uses equal costs, so it cannot tell either.
findings.resolution: Retitle sh6 to what it asserts: the split's order. Add a case that sweeps, at jobs=1, a heavy plain file and a staged fixture whose per-block estimate is higher, with costs given, and reads the order off each row's windows (start times): costliest job first.

findings.issue: replayed() keeps the first entry for a label (by.setdefault) and drops any later one silently. A list naming one block twice - the shape a sweep that ran a block twice would hand over - replays one copy and is never named. The sweep cannot produce that today: labels are unique by stage_labels, paths are set-deduped, and there is one counter per suite. But the replay is meant to be the honest reading, and it names a missing block and a stray block yet not a doubled one.
findings.resolution: Count labels in entries. A label listed more than once becomes one failing case '<label> RAN TWICE'. Add it to sr15's list, red-first by restoring setdefault.

findings.issue: The clause 'at some moment blocks of both run' rests on a-blocks sleeping 0.3 s, measured inside each child after its own interpreter start. It fails whenever b1's sleep starts more than 0.3 s after the last a-block's sleep began. That is start-up jitter, which the executor itself measured at load average 18-20 on 10 cores, and this case runs inside a full sweep's 8 workers. The other clauses (two b blocks at once, never more than four) are robust.
findings.resolution: Lengthen the a nap (for example 1.5 s, still well under b's 3 s), or read concurrency off the rows' per-process windows that sweep() now returns, rather than off in-sleep spans.

findings.issue: RUNNER_LINE_END_PENDING leaves the class open in _runner_output._pytest_cases/_pytest_tally and stamp-verification.final_error, and its comment explains the rows by a task boundary ("files the change that added this lint did not own"), which stops being true the moment another task touches them. The rows have no owner recorded where the next reader will look, and the docstring's own advice (a function handed normalised text should call plain_text itself, since it is idempotent) is not applied to these sites. runner_line_end_violations(pending=()) on the real tree returns exactly these three sites (_runner_output.py:444, :594, stamp-verification.py:728), so the debt is real and measured.
findings.resolution: State the reason in terms of the code (the public caller normalises; final_error strips after matching), not the change that added the lint, and file or name the follow-up task that deletes each row (calling plain_text inside the three functions costs nothing and removes them).

findings.issue: The house_red fixture is built with odd string surgery ("SELFTEST FAILED: 2/3 cases " + "passed\n" and "1/2 files ok, %d cases\n" % (5,)), which reads as a contrivance to get past the prose-number lint and makes the fixture harder to read than the output it imitates.
findings.resolution: Write the fixture as one literal block, or build it from the runner's own formatter if one exists, so the CRLF twin is visibly the same text.

findings.issue: The committed cost table's `about` text still reads 'wall seconds times the slots of the sweep's budget the file held' - the very sentence the task's second med clause lists as false ('record_costs about text ... which --record-costs writes into .github/sweep-costs.json'). The diff corrects the generator (record_costs, tools/sweep-selftests.py) but not the file it wrote, so the repo now carries the retired-model wording until someone re-records. The executor disclosed this and says it was told not to edit the file; nothing in the task description says so.
findings.resolution: Replace the `about` string in .github/sweep-costs.json with the text record_costs now writes (same bytes, no cost values touched), or file a follow-up that re-records the table and names it.

findings.issue: The new duplicate-label failure (replayed() third return value, replay_selftest 'RAN n TIMES') and its case sr18 live in tests/_harness.py, which the recorded gate (`python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tools/sweep-selftests.py`) does not select and tests.add does not name. The executor ran `tests/_harness.py --selftest` (90/90) separately and states sr18 was not proved red by mutation; the gate record therefore says nothing about this low clause.
findings.resolution: Add `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/_harness.py` (or the harness selftest) to the task's tests.gate / list tests/_harness.py in tests.add, and mutate replayed() to the old setdefault-only form once to show sr18 red.

findings.issue: The diff makes the probe a meta.buildCommands key, but phase_gate_default() defaults a NEW phase's gate to EVERY buildCommands key not in meta.phaseGate.exclude (only review-only keys are skipped). Once the orchestrator sets lintProbe, /audit:phase add on a plan without a derived or excluding phaseGate writes `lintProbe` into each new phase's gate, so run-test-gate.py runs the mutating probe with no --changed (the whole probe, minutes, rewriting the tree) as an ordinary gate command. Neither the diff, phase-signoff.md 4b nor any case mentions or pins this; the other side of the boundary is untouched.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.24-6yq (d36d84e800c1): Treat lintProbe as a key that is not a gate entry in phase_gate_default (a reserved set beside REVIEW_ONLY_GATES), with a case in the phase-gate-default suite; or at least state in step 4b that a plan naming lintProbe must list it in meta.phaseGate.exclude.

findings.issue: phase_gate's new docstring says 'each step held to SIGNOFF_STEP_SECONDS', but only run-test-gate.py is handed --timeout; the derive-phase-gate.py call just above it is not bounded by it.
findings.resolution: Reword to say the recorded gate run is held to it, or pass the bound to derive-phase-gate.py if it takes one.

findings.issue: To make the prints fit the byte budget the diff rewrote two step texts that R4 did not name (R4 asked to 'Shorten or merge the clause'). The done rule lost its consequence: 'a parent that is not the development branch does not hold the work yet' became 'Report where it landed, and whether that is the development branch', which no longer tells the agent what to say; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md:956 still describes the note as one the sign-off report must repeat. The not-fast-forward line dropped 'the parent moved'. Only lp7 pins the sizes, not the wording.
findings.resolution: Keep the consequence in the done rule (terse form) and take the bytes from the probe clause or the did-line instead, or add a case pinning the wording the guide promises.

findings.issue: The committed cost table's about text still reads 'wall seconds times the slots of the sweep's budget the file held', which the edited record_costs string (tools/sweep-selftests.py:1624-1630) now contradicts for a block-run suite. The generator and the file it writes disagree until a re-record, and no live task holds that: the tasks that named the re-record and the about text are both cancelled, and no case compares the two.
findings.resolution: File a task that either replaces the about string in the table with the bytes record_costs now writes (no cost values touched) or re-records the table from the Windows cells' logs, and name the file in its scope.

findings.file: tests/_harness.py:805-826 (run's print(text)), reached from replay_selftest at 1232-1262
findings.issue: The replay now escapes what each block PRINTED (res out/err) through encodable, but the replay's own report is still written strictly: run() does print(text) of a _render() whose FAIL lines carry each failing case's label and detail, and those details are text the child produced and the sweep decoded as UTF-8 (a %r or str of a value holding an arrow or U+FFFD). Under the same strict cp1252 stdout a failing replayed case with such a detail still raises out of print(text), hiding the tally behind the same 0/1 the change set out to remove. It only bites when a case is already failing, so a green run is unaffected; sr19 covers the out path only, not a failing detail.
findings.resolution: Write the rendered text through encodable(text, sys.stdout) in run() (or reconfigure the stream with errors=backslashreplace once at the replay's entry), and add a case beside sr19 whose replayed block FAILS with a non-cp1252 detail and still prints the exact tally under PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252.

findings.issue: The ar17 comment says the redo is refused because the commit the read builds is checked against what git status lists in the tree. The refusal ar17 actually sees comes from tree_undescribed (the forced file is staged in the index as neither its base nor the work holds it), because _unheld counts an ignored file the scratch index lacks as held. The executor's own notes say so, and the mutation log agrees: the row 'carry commit trusted, never checked against the files' turns ar17b and ar17c red but not ar17. So ar17 would stay green with carry_commit's status-versus-scratch check deleted, and its title and comment name the wrong layer.
findings.resolution: Reword the ar17 comment and title to say the staged-state question refuses a forced file the read misses, and leave the status-versus-scratch check to ar17b and ar17c. Or point ar17 at a path the read misses that is not ignored, so it reaches carry_commit's check.

findings.issue: CONFIRMED (adversarial probes p3/p4, read against the code). repair_asides decides whether a recorded move happened by os.path.isdir(aside) / os.path.isdir(move['from']), not by git's record (admin/gitdir, the tree's .git file). (a) Aside missing and from present is read as 'never moved' and _take_back_aside runs: if the move did happen (rename done, repair failed, record still locked) and a human then removed the aside and a NEW tree was cut at the task path, take-back write_record()s the OLD record (old base) into the NEW tree's marker (write_record asks admin_dir(from), which is now the new tree's admin) and the unlock goes to the new tree's record, so the old admin stays locked with the drive's reason and the drop of keptTrees/asideMoves forgets it; recut_standing then refuses on base mismatch. (b) Aside and from both missing (human did worktree remove -f -f, or rm -rf of the aside, after a failed repair) returns the 'stands at neither' stop on EVERY drive step, because repair_asides is the first statement of drive_locked and the stop names no way to forget the entry: only hand-editing the drive state frees the drive. Nothing in the stop or the guide names that remedy.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.47-6yq (942899f24f2c): Classify off git's record: read move['admin']/gitdir (the path git still holds for the record) and the .git file of whatever stands at from/aside, and take back only where from's .git file names move['admin']; where it names another admin, treat from as someone else's tree: drop the entry without touching its marker or locks. Give the 'stands at neither' case an exit: when neither path stands and git's record at move['admin'] is gone or prunable, drop both entries with a did-line, or name a verb that does. Add a case for each: a new tree at from after the aside was deleted (marker untouched), and neither path standing (drive proceeds).

findings.issue: CONFIRMED. _take_back_aside drops keptTrees and asideMoves and writes state unconditionally, even when _unlock_moved failed. The drive's lock then stays on git's record with no entry anywhere that names it, so no later step retries; the failure is only a did-line / stop sentence. Consequence: remove_task_tree's git worktree remove --force refuses a locked record (needs -f -f), so that tree is kept forever, and the record is never prunable.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.47-6yq (942899f24f2c): Keep the asideMoves entry (marked as take-back pending) while the unlock has not held, so repair_asides retries the unlock on the next step; drop the entries only once the unlock returned ''.

findings.issue: CONFIRMED. A relpath ValueError (checkout and submodule repository on different drives) is turned into a reason, which _repair_moved_tree returns, and repair_asides turns into a stop on every step, forever: the retry cannot succeed because the same relpath is computed again, and the lock stays on the record. ta13b pins this stop as the wanted outcome. git itself writes an absolute core.worktree when no relative path exists, so the fallback exists.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.47-6yq (942899f24f2c): On ValueError from relpath, write the absolute path (now) to core.worktree instead of returning a reason; keep the reason only for the undecodable-bytes case. Change ta13b to assert the config holds the absolute path and the repair returns ''.

findings.issue: CONFIRMED. The diff puts keys of the form '<id> set aside <n>' into keptTrees; kept_trees_block lists them as taskId and _kept_tree_lines tells the reader to take one down with '/audit:worktree task-remove <taskId>'. manage-worktrees.py do_task_remove:703 answers E_USAGE 'no task ... in this plan' for any id not in the manifest, so the printed remedy for an aside entry cannot work (the sentence also says each holds work the phase tree lacks, which a clean aside kept for a staged index does not). Crosses a boundary the diff changed: both sides named. ta1b asserts only that the path is listed.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.47-6yq (942899f24f2c): In kept_trees_block / _kept_tree_lines render an aside key with the real remedy (keep it until the task closes: the drive offers it to the remover at retire; or remove with git worktree remove after reading it), and add a status case asserting the line for an aside entry does not name task-remove.

findings.issue: The redo now depends on git worktree repair (git 2.30 and later). On an older git the repair exits non-zero after the rename has happened, every redo stops with the record locked, and the retry in repair_asides can never succeed. Nothing checks the git version and no document states the floor (only the merge replay checks one, for another command). The previous mechanism (task-remove) worked on any git.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.47-6yq (942899f24f2c): Check for the verb's presence (or git --version) before the rename and refuse the redo with nothing moved, or state the floor in the guide and doctor; failing before the rename is cheap, failing after it is the wedge of finding 1.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "repair_asides may stop the drive only for a live locked record whose tree is missing": _settle_move's last branch (`if not named or reason != ASIDE_LOCK` ... else `_stopped(aside_missing(...))`) is reached whenever the record is live and drive-locked and names neither `from` nor a held `aside`; it never asks whether the tree the record names exists. A set-aside whose unlock failed, which a human then moved to a third path and repaired with git's own `git worktree repair <third>`, has `named` = third, an existing tree. It stops anyway, saying the tree is "not where git's record names" and that no directory holds it (the docstring says "otherwise the record's tree is missing"). Remedy 1 ("put the tree back at <named>") is a no-op because the tree is already there, so every step re-stops. Remedy 2 (`git worktree unlock <named>` + `prune`) works on the unlock but prune finds the tree, so the next step takes the `reason != ASIDE_LOCK` branch and _forget_move drops the keptTrees entry (the aside path is not standing), orphaning a tree that holds work from status. Confirmed from the code; the same orphaning follows for an unlocked record naming a third path. Probe q1 reproduces it.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.47-6yq (942899f24f2c): Gate the stop on `not os.path.isdir(named)` (or on `_holds_record(named, admin)` being false). When the named tree exists and holds the record, treat it as the moved tree: run `_finish_aside` against `named`, and re-point the kept entry at `named` (state["keptTrees"][key] = named) so it stays listed. Add a case: tree moved to a third path and repaired by hand, then repair_asides finishes it, unlocks, and keeps it listed.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "Name a remedy that works for an aside": the remedy printed for a set-aside is a bare `git worktree remove <path>`. A set-aside is a tree that holds work, and `git help worktree` (git 2.53.0) says remove acts only on clean worktrees; "Unclean worktrees or ones with submodules can be removed with --force". So it refuses a set-aside holding uncommitted work or a submodule checkout. It also fails when git's record is gone: _forget_move leaves a standing aside directory listed (drive-phase.py:4986-4998), and remove fails on a path with no record. kt5 asserts only the spelling of the command, never that it acts, so the case cannot see this.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.47-6yq (942899f24f2c): Name a remover that works on a tree holding work and a submodule, for example `git worktree remove --force <path>`, stated as destroying the work. For a listed aside whose record is gone, name removing the directory. Either run the printed command in kt5 against a real unclean aside, or state in the line that it refuses a tree with work.

findings.issue: The remedy `/audit:phase <phase>, whose next step finishes moving it` is false whenever the next step does not finish the move. _settle_move may take the move back, forget it, or stop (aside_missing) instead. The PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE paragraph repeats the claim.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.47-6yq (942899f24f2c): Word it as `/audit:phase <phase>, whose next step settles the recorded move`, in the line and in the guide.

findings.issue: The read-back remedy offers `git -C <aside> diff --quiet --ignore-submodules=none HEAD` as the command to settle. That command exits 1 on every set-aside holding work, which is the normal case, and _repair_moved_tree itself treats 0 and 1 as success (`code in (0, 1)`). A human running it sees exit 1 and reads it as the failure.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.47-6yq (942899f24f2c): Say that exit 0 or 1 is a read and any other exit is the failure, or drop `--quiet` from the printed command and tell the human to look for the error text.

findings.issue: A run that dies partway through a take-back, or before the lock, yields a false did-line. Marker restored and unlock done but write_state not reached: the next step finds the tree at `from` with the task marker and no lock, so it takes the `marked is not True and reason != ASIDE_LOCK` branch and writes "carries neither the set-aside's marker nor the drive's lock - a tree cut there since", though it is the original tree. The same happens in the common case of a run that died after recording the move and before locking (this is the ta14c path, which passes through _forget_move rather than a take-back and does not check the line). The state ends right; the sentence does not.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.47-6yq (942899f24f2c): Word the did-line for what was observed (`no marker or lock of the drive's was found at <origin>, so the recorded move is dropped`) without asserting a tree was cut since.

findings.issue: An unreadable `locked` file (`_lock_reason` -> `(None, why)`) is treated as `reason != ASIDE_LOCK`, so _settle_move forgets the move (both the first-branch and last-branch forget) while the drive's lock may still be on the record. The did-line quotes `unread`, but the lock is left with no record of whose it is, which is what the take-back change set out to prevent.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.47-6yq (942899f24f2c): When `unread` is non-empty, keep the move recorded and stop naming the file that could not be read, instead of forgetting it.

findings.issue: KEPT_TREE_FORCE understates what the named `git worktree remove --force` destroys. It lists uncommitted, untracked and ignored files and 'each submodule checked out in it', but removing the worktree also deletes git's record directory, so commits that live only in a submodule repository under that record's modules/ directory are lost. This is the very data the task's own case ta11 proves a redo keeps. The tree's detached HEAD commits also become unreachable unless pinned. The tail 'carry what it holds first' does not tell the reader to look for either. Confirmed from the code: the text is the whole warning and mentions neither.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.49-6yq (152b7253f131): Extend KEPT_TREE_FORCE to say it also deletes git's record of the tree, so commits held only in a checked-out submodule's repository and the tree's detached HEAD (if no ref holds it) are lost. Pin kt5 on those words.

findings.issue: With the plan unreadable (task_ids None) the new `_kept_tree_remedy` names `git worktree remove --force` for EVERY kept tree, including a blocked member's tree that close_wave records under its task id (drive-phase.py:5936-5941) and that a later wave adopts by marker. Before the diff, a None plan gave the bare remover, which refuses a tree holding work. Now the one case where status cannot tell a task's tree from a kept old tree gets the destructive command. Confirmed: the only guard is `task_ids is not None and task_id in task_ids`.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.49-6yq (152b7253f131): When task_ids is None, name the safe form (bare `git worktree remove <path>`, or say the plan could not be read and the key cannot be classified) and give the forced form only for a key matching the ` set aside <n>` shape (drive-phase.py _ASIDE_KEY_RE). Add a case for the unreadable-plan row.

findings.issue: The claim 'a path once taken is never cut at again' is stronger than the code. RECUTS is a dict keyed by task id and is not in KEPT_AT_TASK_CLOSE (line 905), so the generic loop at drive-phase.py:8673-8676 pops recuts[task] when the task closes. drop_state removes the whole file when the phase finishes. After that, if every kept tree has been removed, the high-water mark is gone and a later redo can start again at .redo-1. The lexists and git-listing checks stop it landing on a path that still exists, so no tree is overwritten, but a removed path can be reused. ta20b only proves the claim while the recuts entry is present.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.49-6yq (152b7253f131): Either soften the guide and docstring to 'never cut at a path that still holds a directory or a git record', or add RECUTS to KEPT_AT_TASK_CLOSE and state that the mark ends with the phase.

findings.issue: keep_old_tree picks the next key from state['keptTrees'] alone. A tree whose marker already names '<id> set aside <n>' but whose state entry is gone (drop_state at finish, or a forgotten entry) is not seen, so the key can be issued twice, and settle_kept_markers would then read the older tree's marker as a crash of the new redo. Confirmed from the code; reachable only after the state was lost.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.49-6yq (152b7253f131): Also skip a key some wave tree's marker already names, or skip any key whose entry was ever recorded under recuts.

findings.issue: submit_tree reads wave.trees directly and never calls settle_kept_markers, which runs only in drive_locked. A submit that arrives after a redo died between the marker rewrite and the state write is keyed to the old tree, whose marker already names the kept key. Confirmed: no other caller of the settle.
findings.resolution: Call settle_kept_markers (or the marker read) in submit_tree before it resolves the tree, or document that submit is refused until the next drive step.

findings.issue: The sweep's reason for a kept tree says 'the wave driver removes it with `task-remove` after integration', which is false for a kept old tree (its key is no task, and task-remove refuses it). The task's own list named this reader (the sweep's kept-tree reason in _worktrees.py); the executor checked it, called the wording wrong and left it. The sweep is path-agnostic and still keeps the tree, so no work is at risk, but it is the one remedy surface left naming a verb that cannot act on a kept old tree.
findings.resolution: Make the reason depend on whether the marker's taskId is a ` set aside <n>` key, and for that case name `git worktree remove --force <path>` or the driver's retire.

findings.issue: The property this task exists for - a row never writes the checkout - rests on prove() passing cwd=tree, --allow-dirty, worker_env(scratch, tree) and the pre/post byte backstop, and no case reaches any of it. c6 (prove-gates.py, 'THIS SUITE MUTATES NOTHING') forbids the suite from calling prove(), ch2/ch4 replace prove with fake_prove, and grep finds no case naming worker_env, _git_env, _pool_parent, _under_a_checkout or _bytes_or_none. Changing cwd=tree back to REPO, dropping the CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/PWD repoint, or deleting the byte-compare would leave all 52 cases green (read, not run). The 1133 s full run shows it works today; nothing keeps it working.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.51-6yq (163b8a986969): Factor the argv/cwd/env of the redfirst call into a pure function (or make the subprocess runner injectable) and assert in a pw case: cwd is the tree, '--allow-dirty' is in argv, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and PWD equal the tree when present, GIT_DIR-family vars are absent, TMPDIR is the scratch. Add a case for the byte backstop using a stub redfirst in a fixture tree that leaves the file mutated (expects verdict ERROR and the file restored).

findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'Update the docs that say prove-gates mutates the tree and restores each time': this shipped reference (read by the agent driving sign-off) still says 'The probe mutates the working tree and restores it under its own trap', and frames the driver's before/after status+bytes comparison as guarding that. The executor's grep covered only CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md; this file is a doc saying exactly that and was not edited.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.51-6yq (163b8a986969): Reword to: each row mutates and restores a worker tree outside the checkout; the checkout is never written, and the driver still compares git status and file bytes around the run, which now must see no change by construction.

findings.issue: Stale text the diff makes false (both confirmed): the lint_probe docstring says 'the probe mutates the working tree and restores it', and _suite.py's marker comment says 'prove-gates.py edits the working tree for minutes... a concurrent sweep read a half-mutated tree'. No tool calls _suite.hold now (git grep '_suite.hold(' finds only the fixtures in tools/orchestrator-state.py:244/250 and tools/sweep-selftests.py:4773/4781), so the marker readers (sweep-selftests marker_gate, orchestrator-state sweep_line) and hold() itself are live code with no production writer. Also tools/prove-gates.py:2228 and :2968 still say 'a run that mutates the tree' (true only of a worker tree).
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.51-6yq (163b8a986969): Fix the two comments/docstrings in a follow-up task; decide separately whether the marker machinery is retired or kept as the compatibility surface CONTRIBUTING.md now describes. Say 'a worker tree' at prove-gates.py:2228 and :2968.

findings.issue: A file that is staged-new in the checkout (in the index, absent from HEAD) is carried by 'git diff HEAD' but applied without --index, so it is untracked in the worker tree. A lint that walks tracked files (CLAUDE.md says several are derived off what git tracks) sees it in the checkout and not in the worker, so a by-hand run on a dirty tree can prove a slightly different tree than its author is looking at. pw3 covers a staged modification, not a staged addition. Read, not run; irrelevant at sign-off where everything is committed.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.51-6yq (163b8a986969): Apply the patch with 'git apply --index' (or 'git add -N' the added paths in the worker), and give the pw3 fixture a staged-new file.

findings.issue: _ordinary_task_gate's files arm hands every declared file to a path-scoped spelling, docs included; the runner_aware arm filters to suite paths but the ordinary one does not, so a task declaring CLAUDE.md/CONTRIBUTING.md got 'python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tools/prove-gates.py CLAUDE.md ...', which the sweep refuses (exit 2, 'not a suite this sweep covers'), and the task gate was red before any work (P142.50's first judge). Separately, scope --tests-add on a pending task does not re-derive a gate derived from files.
findings.resolution: Filter the ordinary files arm to suite paths as the runner_aware arm does (falling through to the wide gate when none is a suite), and re-derive a files-basis gate when tests.add changes on a task that has not started.

findings.issue: reap_stale discards close_workers' problem list and returns every stale root, so main prints 'took down X' even when _drop_registration or remove_tree failed, and the exit stays 0; only a git worktree list failure exits 2.
findings.resolution: Return what was actually taken down beside what was not, say the failures on stderr, and exit 2 when a stale pool could not be taken down.

findings.issue: On SIGTERM, run_ordered's finally calls pool.shutdown(wait=True), which waits for the rows already running (multi-minute suites); a caller that follows SIGTERM with SIGKILL after a short grace leaves the pool registered until the next run reaps it, so the docstring's 'SIGTERM included' holds only if the caller waits.
findings.resolution: Terminate the running rows' process groups on SIGTERM before shutdown, or state the grace the cleanup needs and check drive-phase's teardown grace against it.

outcome.technical: ONE INVARIANT replaces the per-case index code: `_invariants.owned_index(base_index, source_index, shard_now, shard_parent, phase_id)` returns base_index with the part the phase owns set to what its shard derives - its tasks' fileIndex rows as a SET (owned task ids = those shard_now holds or shard_parent held, so a dropped file or a moved task loses its row; `_owned_rows`), each bug shard_now links whose source entry names the task back (taken whole), and its stub's `_manifest_io._STUB_KEYS` mirrored from the shard (stub taken from source for a new phase); everything else is base_index's bytes unchanged. `index_needs` is deleted. Writer: `_scoped_commit.index_to_carry` only DECIDES (owned_index of HEAD's index vs the working shard); the bytes come from `_scoped_commit.blob_builder`, a builder `stage_blobs(git_root, blobs, head)` runs against the HEAD `stage_and_commit` reads - the parent `commit_from_index` commits onto and refuses to move past - so no window remains (F1). `stage_and_commit`/`commit_with_rows` `blobs` is now `{rel: build}`. Task commit: `with_index` hands the builder. State commit: `state_index` returns (mode, build, notes); whole mode = working index with the owned part derived, needs mode = parent with the owned part derived - both carry the phase's stub (F3); the index no longer counts in `pending`, the decision is state_index's. The answer gains `indexLeft` (what of the index stayed uncommitted and why) and `indexDropped`; close-phase `_commit_stamp` returns `landingCommitLeft` and both renderers print it (`_render_left`); drive-phase `keep_record`/`commit_signoff` add `index left uncommitted: ...` did-lines (`_state_answer`) (F3). Grader: `_commit_carries_needs` = committed == owned_index(parent index, committed index, committed shard, parent's shard).doc, the same function. History (F2): hist2.py over this repo's plan - 15 task commits staged the index; OLD breach set (completed_bug_links rule) = NEW breach set = 14 commits [P15.4 24da908, P18.10 fad5cd9, P2.7 49741c4, P20.6 fad5cd9, P27.1 d04c313130, P53.4/P53.5/P53.6 3fd21d0, P53.9/P54.4/P54.5/P54.6/P54.7 49bacaa, P99.1 8158b402]; new-not-in-old []; P128.38 bdab2ce0c5 clean under both. tasks.title: The affected selection's miss rate is measured on this repository's history before any task gate trusts it
tasks.description: Add tools/measure-affected-miss.py. Mutation half: for each of the last N task commits (default 20), in a scratch worktree at that commit, apply each of two mutations to every changed .py (an import-time raise, and a house-style violation the tree lints read), run the full sweep, and count the suites that went red that tools/affected.py --base <parent> did not select. CI half: for each failed CI run in the window, read its failing suites (gh run view --log-failed) and check them against the selection for that SHA's diff. It prints 'misses M of N commits (mutation); K of J runs (CI)' with every miss named; a CI half that could not ask prints could-not-ask and is never read as zero. It never edits the checkout: every mutation happens in its own scratch worktree, removed in finally. Acceptance: (1) on a fixture repository where a suite depends on a changed module the selection omits, the miss is counted and named; (2) a selection that includes every red suite counts zero misses; (3) no gh, or no network, prints could-not-ask for the CI half; (4) the checkout's status is unchanged after a run; (5) the measured result over 20 commits is recorded in the task outcome with the commit range.

tasks.title: The affected selection names every suite a change can turn red: tree-scanning lints always, and suites reaching a module through a subprocess or a sibling's import
tasks.description:
The P142.3 measurement (tools/measure-affected-miss.py --commits 20, range 17563b1b..4805f994) found that 13 of 16 measured commits had at least one suite turned red by a mutation in a changed file that tools/affected.py did not select. Two classes, not a list of instances:

1. Tree-scanning suites. A suite whose lint walks every tracked file (tests/test__output_lints.py on a style mutation in almost every commit; also test__help_lints, test__deps, test__refs and the like) is affected by ANY change to a file in the set it scans. The selection must derive that set from the lint's own walk (the shared walks in tools/lints) rather than from a hand list, and select the suite whenever a changed path falls inside it.

Raise mutations were missed for suites that reach the module transitively (A imports B imports changed C), through a subprocess of an entry script (`[sys.executable, <script>]`, `_loader`, `find_script`), or by reading its source. Close the reverse-import walk transitively and add the subprocess/loader edges, derived from the code, not spelled.

tasks.title: A task tree follows the phase head when the base moves under it, so a red the phase has since fixed is not charged to the task
tasks.description:
Observed in P142 on 2026-10-26: four returned tasks (their trees based at d4a26f13 / d92b9c64) went gate-red only on a suite that was red at their base; the phase then landed the fix (b10ddfdd), but a `rerun` still ran in the old tree (the run's testedState.head stayed at the old base), so the only exits were an owner override or a pointless retry. The gate judges a task on a base that is no longer the phase's.

Fix the structure: when the drive re-gates (rerun/retry) or before it gates a returned task, and the phase head has moved past the tree's base, bring the task tree to the phase head with the task's work carried - only when none of the task's changed files moved between the two commits (a fast check over `git diff --name-only base..head`); otherwise refuse by name, listing the overlapping files, and leave the tree untouched. Record the base change (old base, new base, the files that moved) in the run's record and in the carry so commit-task-work diffs the task's work against the new base and the stamp/scope digest is unaffected. Never rebase or rewrite a commit; the task tree holds uncommitted work over a detached HEAD, so the move is a checkout of the new head carrying the working-tree changes, verified byte-for-byte on the task's files after the move. Read drive-phase.py's rule "never rebase - it rewrites the task commit SHAs" and keep it true.

Note: task P142.12-6yq has uncommitted work in its own tree that also edits drive-phase.py and tests/test_drive_phase.py (sign-off lint probe); keep your drive-phase change small and local to the gate/dispatch path so the two integrate cleanly.

tasks.description:
`audit-task.py` `_held_dirt` refuses `start` when one of the task's declared files holds an uncommitted change that another blocked/in_progress task with a spent attempt also declares, and `_held_dirt_refusal` offers two ways past: finish that task, or set the change aside with a named stash. Fix the class:
1. A holder whose work lives in its own task tree (its marker/provenance via _worktrees, the same reading the drive uses) cannot be holding the project checkout's change - do not charge it.
2. A change whose bytes match the starting task's own most recent filed return stamp (the scope/dirty digests stamp-verification computes - reuse that function, do not reimplement a digest) is that task's own work: not a refusal.
3. The refusal never names a command any guard in this plugin refuses; drop the stash remedy and name the supported ones (finish/unblock the holder, or commit it).

tasks.description:
Observed in P142 on 2026-10-27, right after the tree-follows-head change landed (862b4941).

P142.13 and P142.14 advanced and went green. P142.12's work overlaps three files the head moved: plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py, tests/test_drive_phase.py and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md. So `advance_member` refused the move by name ("the tree stays at d4a26f13"). The drive then ran the gate in that tree anyway. The gate went red on te11/ln1 in tests/test__output_lints.py, which b10ddfdd had already fixed, and the base verdict was `no-base`. The gate-red decision offered retry|rerun|block. None of those moves the tree, and `redo` is offered only at integration-refused. So the task had no supported exit except a block. This is the same defect the tree-follows-head change was opened to remove, now reached by every task whose files the phase also edits.

Fix the structure:
1. A refused move is not a gate input. When `advance_member` refuses because the work overlaps files that moved, the drive records no gate run on that base. It stops with a decision whose answers include `redo`: recut the tree at the phase head carrying the task's work as a patch, three-way where it applies. Only the task's work paths are carried, never the plan's record files, the same exclusion integration uses. Each carried path is then verified against refs/audit/carry/<task> after applying.
2. A redo whose patch does not apply leaves the old tree and the carry ref untouched. It refuses by name, listing the conflicting paths.
3. Reuse the existing redo machinery (`redo` at integration-refused, the patch it writes and the tree take-down) rather than a second copy. Find the one place the decision table decides which answers a state offers.

Red-first each case. Use a fixture whose work overlaps a moved file and is gated at its old base today (red), and gets the recut decision and no gate row after the fix. Also cover a redo whose patch conflicts (refused, tree and carry ref unchanged), and record files never carried. Prove a failure mid-redo leaves the work as it was.

High risk: it recuts a tree that holds an agent's only copy of its work. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: The sweep reads every child's output with one line end, so no check that counts a line sees Windows line ends
tasks.description:
Observed on CI run 40511735770 (ci/P142 at 94a097d7, release tier), both Windows legs, plain and cp1252: tests/_harness.py sr13 FAIL. The sweep ran the staged suite correctly: ok True, blocks 5, slots 1, pools [], order and tmps as expected. The one conjunct that failed is `out.count(REPLAY_LINE % (5,)) == 1`. REPLAY_LINE ends in "\n". The child writes it through a text-mode stdout, so on Windows it arrives as "\r\n". The sweep decodes the child's bytes as they are (`done.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")` in tools/sweep-selftests.py, where a file's row output is captured), so every row "output" a reader receives keeps Windows line ends.

This is the third time this phase has hit the class. Run-test-gate's readers came first, then the private patterns the runner-line-end lint now covers. Each earlier fix normalised at a reader. Fix it once, where the text enters:
1. Every place tools/sweep-selftests.py turns a child's bytes into text normalises line ends at that point. Reuse the one normalisation the plugin already has (`_runner_output.plain_text`, or the function it calls for line ends) rather than writing a second one. So a row's "output", and every line the sweep itself parses, reads "\n" on every platform.
2. A case that fails on today's code on any platform: a fixture child that writes "\r\n" line ends as raw bytes, run through the sweep. Its row output and the replay count read the same as a "\n" child's. Red-first it on posix by writing the CRLF bytes explicitly, so the case does not depend on the runner's platform.
3. sr13 itself needs no change once the capture normalises. If any other check in tests/_harness.py or tools/sweep-selftests.py counts or compares "\n"-terminated text read from a child some way other than through the sweep's capture, normalise it the same way and list each site in your outcome.

Do not widen the runner-line-end lint in this task. Say in your outcome whether it could see this shape (a str count or endswith on unnormalised child text) and why not. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: Starting a task reads a repeated status row as a repeat, so a holder's duplicated block rows do not keep its own work charged
tasks.description:
Observed in P142 on 2026-10-27, on every restart of a single-dispatch task in the project checkout (three times in a row). `audit-task.py start` refused because another blocked task declares the same files. The release that exists for this case asks `_ran_within(_status_events(...))` whether the holder ran in the window, and it answered None ("cannot tell"). The cause is a real journal holding duplicate block rows: `in_progress->blocked` twice in the same second, then `None->blocked`. Both the drive and audit-task record the block, so the status chain reads as broken. Each time, the orchestrator had to set the work aside by hand, start, and restore it with sha256 checks.

Fix the reading, not the instance:
1. A status row whose `to` equals the state already reached is a repeat, not a break, whatever its `from` says (None included). Collapse repeats before the chain is judged.
2. Keep refusing a chain that is genuinely broken: a `from` that is neither the reached state nor None, or a row naming a different state with no transition into it.
3. Look at why two writers record the same block. If one of them is redundant, say so in your outcome; do not remove a journal writer in this task.

Red-first with the exact row shape copied from the real journal (same-second duplicate plus a `None->blocked`). It must read as "did not run within the window" where that is true. Add an over-fire case: a genuinely broken chain still answers None, and the refusal still fires. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

add: tests/test_audit_task.py: a journal holding a same-second duplicate block row and a None-to-blocked row reads as one transition, and a genuinely broken chain still answers cannot-tell

outcome.technical: Added _status_chain(events) in plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py: folds a row whose `to` equals the reached state into the row that reached it when its `from` is None, the reached state, or the `from` of the row that reached it; returns None when a move-on row does not start at the reached state, or a repeat names any other from. _ran_within now judges that chain instead of the raw adjacent-pair check; its last-event-vs-current check is unchanged. _status_events and _filed_while_running untouched. Tests (tests/test_audit_task.py, after hw11): hw13 real-shaped rows (manifest.edit pending->in_progress, task.block, manifest.edit and task.blocked all in_progress->blocked in the same second, wave.done None->blocked) -> window after block answers False, window straddling the run answers True; hw14 four genuinely broken chains (repeat with a stale other from, None->different state, from a never-reached state, last change not ending at current) all answer None. Mutation: repeat accepting any from -> hw14 red; fix absent -> hw13 red. Gate: sweep of tests/test_audit_task.py 1127 cases ok; tests/test__deps.py 254 ok; tests/test__output_lints.py 173 ok. tasks.title: A build command that runs at sign-off is never defaulted into a phase's gate
tasks.description:
Review finding P142-R22 (med), on P142.12-6yq at its landing. The sign-off lint probe is now named by `meta.buildCommands.lintProbe` (drive-phase.py `LINT_PROBE_KEY`). But `_manifest_phases.phase_gate_default()` defaults a new phase's gate to every `buildCommands` key that `meta.phaseGate.exclude` does not name. The only keys it skips are the review-only ones (`_manifest_vocab.review_only_keys`: the `REVIEW_ONLY_GATES` catalog, plus values starting `review-only:`). So once a plan sets `lintProbe`, `/audit:phase add` on a plan with no excluding `phaseGate` writes `lintProbe` into each new phase's gate. Then run-test-gate runs a probe that mutates the tree, as an ordinary gate step, on every task and phase gate.

Fix the vocabulary, not the one key:
1. A `buildCommands` key can be a sign-off step rather than a gate command. Give the catalog that category beside the review-only one (`lintProbe` is its first member), in `_manifest_vocab`, and make it the one place both questions are answered.
2. `phase_gate_default` skips sign-off-only keys exactly as it skips review-only keys, and its basis names what it skipped.
3. A phase or task gate that names a sign-off-only key explicitly is reported by the plan's validation (validate-manifest), with a message that says the key runs at sign-off and not as a gate step. Find where `_check_phase_gate` warns about an always/exclude overlap and put the check beside it.
4. Any other reader that builds a gate from `buildCommands` keys (grep `buildCommands` for derivations) reads the same predicate.

Red-first each case:
- a plan with `lintProbe` set and no `phaseGate` defaults a new phase's gate without it (red today);
- an explicit gate entry naming it is reported;
- over-fire: an ordinary key is still in the default, and a review-only key is still skipped.
No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: The state commit takes the index lock in a sharded plan, keeps stdout one JSON object, commits on an unborn branch, and commits the shard from the bytes its index part came from

What it fixes, each reproduced before the fix:

tasks.title: A recut drops a task tree only when the carry commit describes that tree completely; any submodule or nested repository refuses it
tasks.description:
A redo removes a task's worktree (`git worktree remove --force`) and recuts it at the phase head with the work re-applied. It can destroy a task's only copy of its work. Defects in it have now been found three times in this phase, each fixed by naming one more shape, so this task fixes it by invariant: the tree is dropped only when the carry commit plus the tree's own index describe it completely, and everything the carry cannot represent refuses the recut before anything is dropped.

Start from the work kept at refs/audit/kept/P142.31-6yq: one commit over the phase head it was cut from; `git diff <its parent> refs/audit/kept/P142.31-6yq` is the whole change. It already does three things: carry_commit seeds its scratch index from the tree's own index, so force-added files are carried; a check compares every path git status lists with the scratch index byte for byte; and _links_touched refuses any change touching mode 160000. Apply it, then make these hold. Each was reproduced by an adversarial review against that work:
1. HIGH: a submodule with `submodule.<name>.ignore=all` (or `diff.ignoreSubmodules=all`) hides its pointer change from git status, from add -A and from the link check. The work reads empty, nothing is pinned, and the remove deletes .git/worktrees/<wt>/modules/<sub> with the submodule's commits. ignore=dirty loses uncommitted edits inside it the same way. Invariant: a tree holding ANY gitlink entry (in its index, its HEAD or the carry) or any nested .git refuses the recut, whatever git's ignore settings say. Every status and diff the check runs uses --ignore-submodules=none.
2. MED, over-fire: `_unheld` runs `ls-files -o` without `--exclude-standard`, so an ignored file untracked with `git rm --cached` (the ordinary node_modules clean-up) is "unheld" forever, and the task can never be filed or redone. Count a path the scratch index lacks and git ignores on disk as held.
3. A staged state the worktree does not show is not carried, and the check cannot notice it, because it compares the scratch index with the worktree only. Two shapes: (a) `git rm --cached` of a tracked file that is not ignored, (b) a staged edit whose worktree copy was reverted (MM). Decide what the work is in each case. The structurally correct answer is that the index is part of the work. Then either carry it or refuse; never drop it silently.
4. Lows, cheap and in the same lines:
   - skip-worktree and assume-unchanged entries are not copied by the seed, so a skip-worktree file absent from disk is carried as a deletion. Copy the flags or refuse.
   - redo_left's fallback text can prescribe an apply over a tree that already holds the work, for a path the head moved.
   - non-UTF-8 path bytes decoded with "replace" become pathspecs that match nothing, so the path reads as held. Keep the bytes.
   - _seed_from_index's docstring overclaims what it copies.

The review's probes are in p142-31-adv/ (the orchestrator gives its full path). Run probe.py through probe4.py before and after. Prove each case red, and deliver a mutation probe with an over-fire row for each refusal. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: Starting a task folds a status row only when it is the hook's echo of the row before it, so a restart the journal missed keeps the charge and the drive's own duplicates still release
tasks.description:
`audit-task.py start` may release a path another task holds when that holder is provably not running. It reads the holder's status chain from the journal (`_status_chain`, `_ran_within`): True means running, False means not running, None means can't tell, and None keeps the charge.

Two attempts have failed in opposite directions:
- P142.22's fold read any later in_progress->blocked row as a repeat, however far apart. That folded away a restart the journal never recorded, and answered False. Fail-open.
- The kept attempt (refs/audit/kept/P142.35-6yq; `git diff <its parent> <ref>` is the whole change) marks the time between a row and its repeat as an unaccounted span and answers None inside it. Over this repo's own journal that over-fires. The drive writes task.block at T. The hook's manifest.edit and task.blocked rows echo the same in_progress->blocked at T+1..9, and the next wave's starts land inside that gap, so they now answer None where HEAD answered False. An adversarial review measured it on docs/audit/journal/*.jsonl: 16 holder/starter pairs, for example P142.14-6yq/P142.15-6yq and P142.4/P142.6.

Fix by provenance, not by time. A row is a duplicate only when it is provably an echo of the row before it: the same task, the same from and to, written by the hook (actor.via "hook") as the derived record of a change whose own row (via cli or a drive verb) immediately precedes it, with no other row of that task between them. Read the real journal to confirm which writers produce which echo, and derive the rule from the code that writes the rows, not from a timing. Fold an echo with no span. Anything else that repeats or breaks the chain answers None.

Also fix, because it is the same ordering: same-second rows from different journal files cannot be ordered (read_all breaks ties by file name), and `_filed_while_running` already says so. `_status_chain` must not read that order as causal; such a pair answers None unless it is an echo pair.

Cases, each red on the right code:
- the real duplicate shape, with a start inside the echo gap: False;
- a lagged repeat with no source row: None;
- the cross-file same-second reversal: None;
- and the existing cases hw11 and hw13-hw16 kept green.
Re-run the review's journal scan (scan.py and near.py in p142-35-adv/; the orchestrator gives its full path) before and after, and report the counts. Deliver a mutation probe with over-fire rows. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: Every forced removal of a task tree asks the one predicate the recut asks, so retiring a closed member never deletes a submodule commit or a nested repository
tasks.description:
P142.40 made the recut ask one predicate, `tree_undescribed(tree, records, work)`, before it drops a tree. The predicate refuses on:
- any gitlink in the tree's index, at HEAD or in the work;
- any `.git` below the tree top, found by walking the disk;
- a staged state the work lacks.
Its status and diffs use --ignore-submodules=none.

Another path still force-removes a tree on a weaker reading. Retiring a closed member runs `retire_member`, then `tree_holds_only_integrated`, then `task-remove --force`. That reads git status without --ignore-submodules=none and compares files with open(). So a submodule commit, a submodule set to ignore=all, or a nested repository in that tree reads as "held" and is deleted with the tree.

Make the invariant live at the choke point, not at each caller. Find every code path that removes a task tree with force: drop_tree, task-remove --force callers, retire, close or sweep paths in drive-phase and in the worktree scripts it calls. Make each go through one function that asks the predicate, together with "is everything the tree holds already integrated or carried", and refuses otherwise. List every such path in your outcome, with the line that routes it.

If a path lives in a file outside this task (plugins/audit/scripts/git/_worktrees.py, manage-worktrees.py), name it in your outcome and do not edit it. The orchestrator will widen the scope.

Cases red on today's code for retire. Each refusal gets an over-fire case: a clean integrated tree still retires. Deliver a mutation probe. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: No drive step destroys a task tree it cannot prove empty of work: a redo sets the old tree aside, and every forced removal goes through one function that keeps the tree on any doubt
tasks.description:
The redo/recut and the retire of a closed member both force-remove a task worktree (`git worktree remove --force`). Four review rounds this phase have each found another shape the pre-removal check missed: force-added files, moved submodule pointers, ignore=all submodules, staged-only states, nested repos on retire. Each round's tightening then over-fired.

The kept P142.40 (landed before this task) made the recut ask one strict predicate, `tree_undescribed`. Its review found no path to loss but three over-fires:
- any gitlink refuses, even a submodule never initialised in the task tree, so a repo with a submodule can never redo;
- `carry_commit`'s `_unheld` check with --ignore-submodules=none refuses when an initialised submodule has build output inside it. Then `refs/audit/carry/<id>` is never written at filing, and that ref is the backup the gone-tree refusal points humans to. Regression;
- integrate-task.py `task_changes` runs `git add -A` in the member tree's real index, so after a human settles an integration conflict by editing, the redo refuses on "staged as neither base nor work holds it". Redo is the answer to integration-refused.
Retire still uses the weaker `tree_holds_only_integrated`, which deletes nested repos and submodule commits.

Remove the class instead of tuning the predicate a fifth time:
1. A redo never deletes the old tree. It sets the tree aside (a path the drive records, beside the task's tree path; mind that `git worktree move` refuses trees with submodules, so choose a mechanism that works for every tree) and cuts the new tree at the task's path. Everything after that is the existing recut. The set-aside tree is listed in the redo's did-line and in `status`.
2. Exactly one function in drive-phase force-removes a task tree. It asks `tree_undescribed` together with "is everything this tree holds integrated or carried". On any doubt it KEEPS the tree, says so in a did-line naming why, and does not stop the drive. Route retire, the set-aside cleanup and any other remover through it, and list each path with its line. A remover in a file outside this task (`_worktrees.py`, `manage-worktrees.py`) is named in the outcome, not edited.
3. With nothing destroyed on doubt, relax the over-fires to what could actually be lost:
   - an unchanged, uninitialised gitlink holds nothing;
   - a submodule's own dirt is not the task's work, and must not stop the filing's carry. Say in the did-line that it was left;
   - an index state superseded by the disk, as after the integrator's `git add` then an edit, is not work.
   Keep the strict reading only where a remove would follow.
4. `tree_undescribed`'s docstring says ignored files are not part of what it describes.

Cases red on today's code for each item. Each keep-on-doubt gets an over-fire twin: a clean integrated tree is removed. Deliver a mutation probe. The review that motivated this is p142-40-adv/ (the orchestrator gives its full path). No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: A status row folds as the hook's echo only inside the tool call that wrote its verb row, and a derived row only straight after its own edit row
tasks.description:
P142.41 made `_status_chain` fold a repeated status row only when `_echoes` proves it is the journal-writes hook's record of the preceding verb row: same from/to, via hook, a shared session. An adversarial review found a fail-open left in it. The report and repro.py are in p142-41-adv/; the orchestrator gives the full path.

1. MED. The first branch reads no time, so a same-session hook row that repeats in_progress->blocked hours later folds as an echo. Per `_pre_seed_sweep` in hooks/journal-writes.py, a hook row's `from` is the file as of the start of its own tool call. So a `from: in_progress` on a hook row whose call began after the verb row proves the task was running again, and that restart is exactly what the journal is missing. The plugin's own writers can lose it: 118 hook manifest.edit rows are truncated, and their clipped changes lists dropped status changes.
2. LOW. The second branch (a derived task.blocked/task.complete after its own edit row) never checks adjacency or the moment, only that the previous event for the task is a hook edit in the same file and session.

Bind both branches to the mechanism. An echo is written at the end of the same tool call as its verb row, so it falls inside that call's duration. Derive the bound from the code: the hook runs at PostToolUse, and the longest call the plugin's tools allow is the Bash tool's timeout cap. Name the constant where it comes from, and do not hand-pick a number. The real journal's largest verb-to-echo gap was measured at 576 s (P128.19-0h5); re-measure it with the review's scan. A derived row folds only straight after its own edit row, at the same moment, in the same file. Anything else answers None.

The review also found two cross-session echoes, written by another session's hook a few seconds after the verb row (P123.35, P123.79-64p). They now answer None where they used to answer False. Judge whether a cross-session echo inside the bound is provable from what the rows record. If it is not, keep None (fail-closed) and say so.

Cases red on today's code; every real echo in docs/audit/journal still folds (re-run the review's scan1.py and gaps.py and report the counts). Deliver a mutation probe with over-fire rows. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: repair_asides classifies a recorded move by git's record, so it never wedges the drive or takes back over a new tree
tasks.description:
A redo sets the old task tree aside: it records the move, locks git's record of it, renames the tree, and repairs. repair_asides runs at the start of every drive step and finishes any move still recorded. It chooses between "never moved", "moved" and "stands at neither" by which directory exists. It never asks git's own record. Adversarial probes in scratchpad/p142-43-adv/r2/ (the orchestrator gives the full path) reproduce two failures:
- p3.py: a failed repair is followed by a human deleting the aside, with its record. Every later drive step then stops with "put the tree at <aside>", which is impossible. That wedges the whole phase, and no answer reaches it.
- p4.py: a half-held repair (repair succeeded, a submodule repoint failed), then the aside is deleted and a new tree is cut at the task path. The next step rewrites the new tree's marker with the old record, says "taken back", and leaves the old record locked.
Fix by invariant: a recorded move is classified by git's record.
- No admin dir: the record is gone, so forget the move with a did-line and never stop.
- Take back only when admin_dir(from) is the recorded admin and its gitdir names `from`.
- Repair only when the recorded admin is the record.
- repair_asides may stop the drive only for a live locked record whose tree is missing. Its remedy must name an action that exists.
Same functions, low:
(a) _take_back_aside drops its entries even when its unlock failed, so the drive's own lock outlives the move (p2.py). Keep a record until the unlock holds.
(b) _repoint_module stops forever when os.path.relpath cannot relate two drives. Write an absolute core.worktree there, as git does. aside_unread's remedy names the step that failed (the repoint or the read-back), not `git worktree repair`, which succeeds by hand.
(c) `git worktree repair` needs git 2.30. Check the floor before the set-aside and refuse the redo with a clear stop, rather than after the rename.
(d) audit-status lists a set-aside key under KEPT TREES with the remedy `task-remove <taskId>`, which cannot act on that key. Name a remedy that works for an aside.
Red-first a case for each of the two failures and for (a)-(d). No F/P/BUG ids in comments.
